title: The AMDGCN Evaluation half exists in parts -- HIP host admission, exact-HIP runtime custody and rocprofv3 trace projection -- and is not yet reachable from a Candidate's admission, launch or timing

evidence.note: The survey that establishes the timing and cache facts an AMDGCN evaluation half would have to be built on: torch.cuda.Event is unusable at 8.48 us empty-interval overhead against 3-7 us kernels; rocprofv2 --kernel-trace supplies per-dispatch nanosecond Start_Timestamp/End_Timestamp together with LDS, SCR, Arch_VGPR, ACCUM_VGPR, SGPR and Wave_Size; hipprof --hip-trace is a second source; rocprofv3 is absent from the image. L2 flush has no HIP API, costs 243.8 us as a 256 MiB zero_(), and measurably changes the answer only below about 4 MiB per buffer.

The other half of the gap, measured: the Compiler already lowers and compiles a gfx938 Schedule to an hsaco and the emitted wrapper matches a reference across five input distributions on one BW1101. Nothing in the Evaluation layer can take that artifact.

The sealed DCU baseline this evaluation path was built against: a 5800-byte HSACO and 19 KB of AMDGCN assembly, with a manifest declaring one hidden scratch pointer. The evaluation itself has not run on the device; bw1100 has been unreachable from the development host for hours at a time.

observation: Corrected twice. The first record said the Evaluation layer had only a CUDA and a Metal half; the second added that tools/capture_executor_host.py's --kind admitted only cuda and metal. Both were read from a stale origin/main ref before the pull, and both are wrong about the current tree. What is actually there: capture_executor_host.py admits hip and amd host kinds and builds a schema v2 host document; lab/executor.py carries HipHostAdmission with its amd-smi, build-tool, profiler and runtime-library closures and admits them without querying a device; evaluation/triton_hip.py owns exact-HIP runtime custody for generated Triton kernels, including admit_exact_hip, hsaco and amdgcn artifact records and an AMDGCN resource record; and evaluation/rocprofv3.py projects rocprofv3 kernel-trace CSV, kernel-stats CSV and results JSON fail-closed, cross-checking the three surfaces against each other. 50 contract tests cover them. What is still missing is the connective tissue rather than the mechanisms. evaluation/artifacts.py::executable_role maps a target to an executable role and knows only metal_binary_archive and cubin, so no gfx target has one and _BUILD_ROLES has no hsaco entry; it now refuses in its own class rather than in CUDA's words, which makes the absence legible without filling it. The schema v2 identity regex pins gfx1151 while the Compiler target on this branch is gfx938, so the two AMD efforts do not yet meet. And the timing path that a paired evaluation selects is still 'metal' or 'cupti' in evaluation/paired.py, with no third name for a rocprofv3 trace. A DCU Executor descriptor can now be captured; a gfx938 Candidate still cannot be admitted, launched, correctness-checked or timed through the common path. The connective parts named above are now in, and running the real entry point named four more. `tasks/evaluate.py` dispatched on `isinstance(manifest, MetalTensorLaunchManifest)` and otherwise `observe_exclusive_cuda` -- but a CUDA and an AMDGCN candidate share that manifest class, both being `workload_tensors_v1`, so the family has to come from the executable the target builds. `allowed_artifact_roles` returned the CUDA role set for anything not Metal. `main` passed collect_timing=True unconditionally, so every search evaluation timed, including on a target with no named timer. Attribution was reached by the same not-Metal path and would have handed a DCU candidate to Nsight Compute. There was also no HIP launch driver at all: `LoadedTorchTensorCandidate` named `LoadedCudaCandidate` and the cubin role directly, so the whole tensor-tile evaluation path -- oracle, cohorts, receipts, none of which is CUDA's -- could only ever run a CUDA candidate.
proposed_change:
Finish the connective tissue rather than rebuilding the mechanisms. Give executable_role and _BUILD_ROLES an AMDGCN entry so an hsaco is a build product the layer knows, keeping the refusal in its own class for every target that has none. Name the rocprofv3 timing path alongside metal and cupti where a paired policy selects one, so a trace is a declared measurement source rather than an unnamed third case. Decide whether the schema v2 executor identity is pinned per AMD target or to AMD generally: gfx1151 and gfx938 are both AMD and only one is in the regex. None of this is a calibration: rocprofv3 gives per-dispatch nanosecond timestamps and the L2 flush is a measured 256 MiB device write, but timing-model coverage for any AMD target remains unavailable until that target has its own. Implemented on this branch: executable_role and _BUILD_ROLES gained an AMDGCN entry keyed on a declared AMDGCN_TARGETS set, so an hsaco is a build product the layer knows and every target without one is still refused in the layer's own class; the schema v2 Executor identity is built from that same set instead of a gfx1151 literal, so both AMD targets are admissible and a third vendor's is not; the host kind field is one field, `kind`, rather than `kind` for Metal and `runtime_kind` for HIP; and the paired policy's measurement source is a declared map rather than `'metal' if ... else 'cupti'`, so CUPTI is named rather than reached by falling through. No rocprofv3 paired kind is minted: nothing produces one yet, and a measurement name with no measurement behind it is the syntax-without-effects this project refuses. That, an AMD evaluation driver that turns an admitted hsaco into a launched dispatch, and a per-target timing calibration are what remain.

Implemented since: `evaluation/hip_driver.py` as the AMDGCN peer of `cuda_driver.py`, deliberately smaller (no cluster attributes, no binary-version check, no dynamic-shared opt-in threshold, none of which is a fact about an amdgcn-amd-amdhsa-- object) and with two deliberate absences -- no soname, because the admitted ROCm PyTorch has already loaded whichever fork this host installs, and no hipFuncGetAttribute, because the kernel's own .amdgpu_metadata already carries its register and scratch counts. `HipDeviceAdmission` and `observe_local_hip` as the allocation half, reading the device contract off `triton_route` rather than a new request field. The local broker serializes per device family, so a DCU run is not recorded under a `metal-` job id. What remains owed is the device-side run: every refusal each of these owns is host-tested, and nothing has yet launched an HSACO through this path on a DCU.
verification_plan: Capability finding, so verification is by campaign. It cannot begin before a released Compiler successor carrying gfx938 and a DCU Executor captured in the container from its exact Python 3.10.12, PyTorch 2.11.0 (HIP 6.3.26113), Triton 3.6.0 and dcc 25.10.0. With both, run the common correctness matrix for one fixed-shape Workload across every declared input case on triton-dcu, then an end-to-end evaluation in the target framework, and compare against a frozen per-task baseline bundle so baseline movement and candidate headroom are reported separately. A passing host-side test suite is not evidence for any of this.
